items.title: Carney’s pipeline push is unlikely to bring back Canada’s oil jobs boom
items.author: Amanda Stephenson
items.creator: Amanda Stephenson
items.summary: Even Mark Carney won’t call it a boom. While Canada’s oil output may rise, experts don’t expect to see major job creation.
items.body:
A Syncrude oil sands plant outside the Alberta oil hub of Fort McMurray, seen from a helicopter. Alberta's oil sands contain one of the world's largest unconventional petroleum reserves in a thick, sticky form of oil called bitumen. Canada's Prime Minister, Mark Carney, wants to export more oil to Asia to blunt the impact of President Donald Trump's tariffs. REUTERS/Todd Korol Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney is betting a new pipeline can help revive the country’s oil industry, boost its production and exports, and reduce its dependence on the United States.
Bringing back jobs will be much harder.
In the Alberta oil hub of Fort McMurray – nicknamed Fort McMoney in its heyday more than a decade ago – the tens of thousands of oil field jobs that powered the last boom are unlikely to return, even if Carney gets his pipeline.
Instead, much of the growth in oil sands output is likely to come from automation and efficiency gains rather than large-scale hiring, according to industry forecasts and nearly a dozen interviews with company officials, workers, politicians and academics.
The pipeline backed by Carney would transport 1 million barrels of crude oil a day to a port on the Pacific coast, expanding export capacity to Asia.
Asked by Reuters what the pipeline would mean for the region’s economy, Carney – a former central banker – cautioned against anticipating a return to the oil-boom days.
"I wouldn't use the term 'boom'," Carney said during a visit to Fort McMurray this month. "I would use ‘sustained growth’."
A giant dump truck hauls unprocessed oil at a Suncor mine near Fort McMurray, Alberta. REUTERS/Todd Korol A construction worker on the job at a new commercial building in the Alberta oil sands hub of Fort McMurray. REUTERS/Todd Korol MORE OIL, FEWER WORKERS More oil without many more permanent jobs could leave Carney politically exposed on two fronts: Critics on the left say his efforts to fast-track the project’s regulatory approval risks sacrificing the environment, while those on the right argue the deregulation should deliver faster economic growth, higher salaries and more oil jobs.
Low job growth could also further fuel Alberta’s separatist movement, though a referendum on whether to hold a vote to leave Canada is expected to fail on Monday.
An August labor forecast by industry group Energy Safety Canada projects that oil sands employment will fall by 920 jobs or 4% by 2035, even as production grows 6%.
A spokesperson for Energy Safety Canada told Reuters that a new West Coast pipeline would likely reverse the projected job decline but may not add many permanent jobs because of the “structural trend” of producing more oil with fewer workers.
"Nobody should expect that something that happened 15 years ago will happen the same way today," said Dianna De Sousa, CEO of the Fort McMurray Chamber of Commerce.
A spokesperson for Carney declined to comment on the lackluster projections for job creation from the pipeline, referring questions to the Department of Natural Resources, which did not respond.
FROM BOOM TO BUST TO WILDFIRES From 2000 to 2014, Canadian and international oil companies spent billions to build out the mega-mines and other facilities required to extract bitumen, the thick oil found in northern Alberta.
Fort McMurray became a place where workers fresh out of high school could earn six-figure salaries, putting new pickups and pricey boats in their driveways.
A boarded-up hotel for sale offers a reminder of the downturn in Fort McMurray's fortunes. REUTERS/Todd Korol Colorful trees grow in a burnt-out forest outside Fort McMurray. REUTERS/Todd Korol A new community of houses in Fort McMurray. Housing values have declined sharply over the last decade. REUTERS/Todd Korol Rush-hour traffic on a major downtown street in Fort McMurray. REUTERS/Todd Korol A delivery driver walks to a store in downtown Fort McMurray. REUTERS/Todd Korol Sarah Thapa, owner of Avenue Eatery and Cafe in Fort McMurray. REUTERS/Todd Korol Guests look at a display in the local Oil Sands Museum. REUTERS/Todd Korol Fly-in, fly-out workers — some from as far as 5,000 km (3,107 miles) away – packed on-site work camps because the city lacked housing.
Then came the 2015 oil price crash, followed by a devastating wildfire one year later. Investors’ growing focus on environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria combined with the climate policies of Carney's predecessor Justin Trudeau deepened the slump.
Nobody should expect that something that happened 15 years ago will happen the same way today.
Dianna De Sousa, CEO of the Fort McMurray Chamber of Commerce
International oil majors exited. Annual oil sands capital investment fell from a C35billion(24.55 billion) peak in 2014 to C$14.2 billion in 2024, according to Statistics Canada. The last major new oil sands project, Suncor's Fort Hills, started up in 2018.
Alberta’s oil and gas sector employs 435,000 people today, including temporary and part-time workers, 85,000 fewer than in 2014, according to data from Alberta’s Servus Credit Union. Real disposable income in the province is still 10% below 2014 levels. Housing values have declined sharply.
Stronger oil prices and rising production have brought some signs of recovery, including regional population growth for the first time in a decade. But flights from Calgary and other major cities sometimes arrive nearly empty, and vacant commercial spaces dot downtown.
"Things are not getting better," said Jenny Parsons, who has worked as a truck driver and contractor at oil sands sites since moving from Newfoundland 15 years ago.
She said she was earning barely a dollar more an hour than she was in 2011.
Jenny Parsons says her wages have flatlined since the boom collapsed over a decade ago. She will vote yes on Monday to holding a referendum on Alberta separation. REUTERS/Todd Korol WHAT A PIPELINE COULD BRING No oil sands company has committed the C$100 billion in private investment needed to fill the proposed pipeline and build the carbon capture and storage project Carney has made a condition of federal approval.
Kendall Dilling, head of the Oil Sands Alliance, which represents the five largest companies, said the projects could create thousands of jobs across Canada by the mid-2030s, including upstream investment and supply-chain activity as well as pipeline construction. But many of these jobs would be temporary construction jobs, in British Columbia as well as Alberta, rather than permanent oil-industry jobs.
Some of those jobs no longer exist. Efficiency gains, for example, have cut the time oil companies spend on routine maintenance, which has reduced the number of staff as well as contract positions, he said.
The employment gains “may be less than the absolute peaks that we've seen in the past.”
Jason Kenney, Alberta's conservative premier from 2019 to 2022, cut corporate taxes to get oil sands companies to spend on big projects. But even after oil prices rose and revenue stabilized, companies prioritized shareholder returns over job growth, he told Reuters.
"I was certainly frustrated with them,” he told Reuters. He said he urged companies to allocate some of the tax cut savings to their capital plans.
"The people need to see a benefit, not just the shareholder in New York."
A Suncor oil sands mine outside Fort McMurray. The company launched the last major new oil sands project in the area in 2018. REUTERS/Todd Korol The industry group representing oil companies did not respond directly to Kenney's comments but said the pipeline provided an opportunity to increase production, create jobs and grow government revenue.
CARNEY FACES RISKS FROM LEFT AND RIGHT By backing a new pipeline, Carney — who grew up in Alberta's capital of Edmonton — has brokered an uneasy truce between the federal government and Alberta conservatives. But he has angered some in his own Liberal party by embracing oil to help the Canadian economy survive President Donald Trump’s tariffs.
He has repealed many of Trudeau's environmental policies, cut the tax rate on new capital investment, and is promoting Canadian oil to investors abroad.
While Carney’s approval rating was at 62% in a September poll from Angus Reid, public sentiment on energy and the environment can shift quickly.
"It's important to remember that the environmental policies of Justin Trudeau were widely popular at the time," said Lori Williams, a political science professor at Calgary’s Mount Royal University. "If we see more environmentally friendly options starting to come on in the future then I think additional pipelines in Canada will be much harder to sell."
Fort McMurray's boom had its downsides. The flood of workers strained local infrastructure and created tensions between locals and the thousands of people in work camps. Some oil sands companies now hire more locals to reduce their reliance on fly-in workers, a shift that reflects a leaner but steadier industry.
Still, longtime residents like Colin Hartigan, owner of the city’s Coldwell Banker United office, hope that Carney's ambitions will bring back at least an echo of the old Fort McMurray.
"At some point, there's going to be another boom," Hartigan said. "Do I think families here want to see that? Not like in the past, that was a little bit crazy. But do we all pray for it? Absolutely."
The Suncor oil sands mine outside Fort McMurray. The company is one of the major producers in the oil patch. REUTERS/Todd Korol
items.raw_description: Even Mark Carney won’t call it a boom. While Canada’s oil output may rise, experts don’t expect to see major job creation.

items.title: France counts cost of worst unrest in years
items.author: Sybille de La Hamaide
items.creator: Sybille de La Hamaide
items.summary: One demonstrator died, hundreds of police were injured and nearly 1,800 people arrested while violent fringe groups targeted public buildings and looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets.
items.body:
France woke on Sunday to the wreckage of one of its most violent days of unrest in years after protests over high prices and public services left one demonstrator dead, hundreds of police injured and nearly 1,800 people arrested.
Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.
One protester died after suffering a cardiac arrest during [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"demonstrations"] in Paris, where police made a record 855 arrests. Across France, more than 500 officers were injured, the interior minister said.
"It's like a war zone here," said Dutch entrepreneur Tije De Boer, who had come to Paris with his children to visit a friend and said the protests forced him to evacuate his hotel at Place de la Republique, which suffered major damage on Saturday.
More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities, marking the convergence of a month-long [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"student movement"] with broader social discontent against rising living costs and declining public services.
President Emmanuel Macron will address the nation at 2000 local time (1800 GMT) on Sunday, his office said.
SEVERAL HUNDRED SHOPS DAMAGED While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers.
A massive clean-up operation began in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said several hundred shops had been damaged on Saturday.
In Paris, smashed shop windows, burnt-out bicycles and spray-painted slogans bore witness to a day that began largely with peaceful demonstrations but descended into violence.
In [USN:L1N46402C TEXT:"Limoges"], southwestern France, mayor Guillaume Guerin denounced the chaos after the city's 143-year-old town hall was set ablaze and partially destroyed in an arson attack on Saturday, drawing comparisons to the 2019 fire that devastated Paris's Notre-Dame Cathedral.
"There was a clear, premeditated intention to burn down the town hall, and the people inside feared for their lives," Guerin told Reuters. He threatened to resign if the city did not receive the million euros needed to repair the city hall.
The unrest has increased pressure on President Macron and his government, with a presidential election due next year. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals.
Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support on Sunday for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement.
Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave said up to 100 stores had been looted in his city, while Marseille Mayor Benoit Payan announced emergency financial aid to support those businesses impacted by the violence.
French retailer Carrefour's <CARR.PA> Chief Executive Alexandre Bompard told BFMTV that 50 of the company's shops had been damaged including 20 that were looted, with losses from the damage running into the dozens of millions of euros.
The protests began last month over school conditions and teacher shortages in working-class suburbs, before broadening into a movement against inequality, public spending cuts and the rising cost of living.

items.title: Japan PM Takaichi's support rate falls below 50%, lowest since taking office, Kyodo reports
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The approval rating for Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration fell below 50% to its lowest level since she took office in October last year, Kyodo News Agency reported on Sunday.
items.body:
The approval rating for Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration fell below 50% to its lowest level since she took office in October last year, Kyodo News Agency reported on Sunday.
In a poll conducted between October 17 and 18, the approval rating for Takaichi's administration was 49.1%, the report said.
The decline might have been affected by Takaichi's slow response surrounding the resignation of Kazuo Yana as the nation's farm minister, the report said.
Yana [USN:L6N4600KT TEXT:"stepped down"] from the post on Wednesday after coming under fire for remarks about cutting road funding for municipalities that did not support him.
Some 57.7% of respondents said Takaichi's decision to replace him came "too late," Kyodo said, while 81.5% said it was natural for Yana to resign.
Takaichi appointed Yana in a cabinet reshuffle last month, but had openly chided him in parliament for the remarks over the road funding, which local media first reported earlier this month.

items.title: Australia's Smith says head blow left him anxious in first test concussion scare
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Australia batsman Steve Smith said he was anxious after being hit on the head and facing the prospect of another concussion after a blow playing against South Africa in the first test a week ago.
items.body:
Australia batsman Steve Smith said he was anxious after being hit on the head and facing the prospect of another concussion after a blow playing against South Africa in the first test a week ago.
Former captain Smith has previously suffered multiple concussions in his career, and he had to go through concussion protocols after a bouncer from Anrich Nortje hit him on the helmet last Monday during the second-last day of the clash at Kingsmead in Durban.
“I was a little bit anxious after the hit, to be honest,” Smith said on Sunday before the start of the second test at St George’s Park in a television interview.
“It was a decent knock, and the rest of that day, I wasn't travelling too well, and I think it was more to do with anxiety, of hoping not to feel what I felt in the past, waking up the next morning and things like that.
“So, yeah, fortunately, I woke up well. I passed all the tests, and things recovered pretty quickly,” Smith added as he prepared to take part in the rain-delayed second test.
The 37-year-old was assessed on the field by the physio and the doctor, and his helmet was changed as is mandatory for all such hits, but he continued his innings, scoring 27 runs as Australia built a large lead.
PASSED CONCUSSION PROTOCOLS But then Smith did not take to the field at the start of South Africa's second innings on Monday, instead being subjected to the concussion protocols, which he passed.
He returned from the start of the last day’s play on Tuesday to help his side to a 214-run victory and a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.
Smith, who is 28 short of 11,000 test runs, was the first player replaced in a test after the introduction of a concussion substitute. He was struck on the back of the head by a Jofra Archer bouncer in the 2019 Ashes test at Lord's in London.
He also suffered a concussion after being hit on the head in practice during Australia's One Day International series in England in 2020 and two months later, back home in Sydney, woke on the morning of the second ODI against India with vertigo and was sick.
There have also been incidents in Sri Lanka in 2022, at the last World Cup in India and last December in the Ashes at Adelaide where he was ruled out of the third test about 20 minutes before the toss with a vestibular issue, the sensory system located in the inner ear that controls balance and spatial orientation.

items.title: Hurricanes riding high but not looking past league-worst Flames
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes are riding a seven-game winning streak and sitting atop the Eastern Conference standings.
items.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes are riding a seven-game winning streak and sitting atop the Eastern Conference standings.
Even so, the defending Stanley Cup champions are not patting themselves on the back as they head to Calgary to face the struggling Flames.
The Hurricanes extended their run with a 3-2 comeback victory over the Winnipeg Jets on Saturday to open a five-game road trip, but they admit it was far from their best.
"We know we've got a lot better than we did (Saturday)," said forward Nikolaj Ehlers, whose power-play goal broke a 2-2 tie in the third period. "We're not exactly where we want to be, but it's a long season, and we've got a lot of time to keep making the small details better."
The win may not have been a masterpiece, but the potency of the Hurricanes lineup was on display.
In a game their top three point producers -- Sebastian Aho, Andrei Svechnikov and Jackson Blake -- were all held off the scoresheet, the Hurricanes converted both power-play opportunities with the depth players stepping forward.
Ehlers and Jesperi Kotkaniemi scored their first goals of the season. Mark Jankowski extended his goal streak to six games, tying the franchise record since its relocation to Carolina from Hartford, Conn., for the 1997-98 season.
Jankowski, who was drafted by the Flames in the first round in 2012 and set a career high with 17 goals in 2017-18 -- the first of his three full seasons in Calgary -- is trying to take his hot streak in stride.
"It just feels great to help the team win any way possible," he said. "That's always been my philosophy. (I'm) just trying to do all the little things right and then eventually, the goals and all that come after."
As the Flames are kicking off a four-game homestand, they sit at the bottom of the league standings.
Calgary has managed only one win in seven outings, with all six defeats in regulation time. The team is back in action after suffering a 6-2 road loss to the Vegas Golden Knights on Thursday.
The Flames fell behind on the game's first shot 25 seconds into the tilt and never recovered.
"Take those puck-play mistakes or mishaps out of the equation, we did a lot of good things in the first period," coach Ryan Huska said. "But you're down 2-0 and against good teams, you can't give them leads like that where we're sitting."
The Flames have dropped all three home games so far this season.
The Vegas loss was even more deflating after Calgary had put together some solid performances, even in defeat, and was coming off its lone victory of the campaign, 4-2 at Anaheim on Tuesday.
"We proved the two games prior we can play a really structured game," said defenseman Jake Middleton, who scored his first goal of the season in the loss. "We didn't (on Thursday) and it's something we can take as a lesson."
Among the myriad reasons for Calgary's struggles is the sudden issue of penalties. The Flames were short-handed five times in each of the past two games, a trend in the first couple of outings that sent their season into a skid.
"You take five or six penalties a night, you're not winning," Huska said. "There are quality players on the ice for too many minutes where they're able to touch the puck. It's not a good thing and it's not a recipe for success."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Congo confirms Ebola outbreak has spread to eighth province
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, Congo's public health institute said on Sunday, confirming earlier Reuters reporting.
items.body:
The Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, Congo's public health institute said on Sunday, confirming earlier Reuters reporting.
The emergence of cases in the province, which borders Central African Republic, poses a new challenge for health authorities struggling to contain the outbreak.
The National Institute for Biomedical Research confirmed two cases - including one death - in North Ubangi.
Reuters [USN:L6N461199 TEXT:"reported on Thursday"] that two cases were confirmed in the province, citing two health officials. At the time, there was no official statement by Congolese authorities.
North Ubangi becomes the eighth province affected by the outbreak, alongside North Kivu, Ituri, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, Sud-Kivu, Bas-Uele and South Ubangi.
The outbreak, the worst Ebola epidemic in Congo's history, has already spread beyond the country's borders, with cases recorded in Uganda and seven infections [USN:L8N4621HW TEXT:"confirmed in Kenya"] this month.
Congo's latest situation report showed 67 new confirmed cases and 26 new deaths in the 24 hours to Oct.16, bringing the cumulative total to 9,415 cases and 4,536 deaths since the outbreak began.
The outbreak remains concentrated in eastern Congo, with Ituri province reporting 44 of the 67 new cases.

items.title: Blue Jackets try to build on success with road game vs. Wild
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Columbus Blue Jackets will seek their first winning streak of the young season on Sunday when they face the Minnesota Wild in Saint Paul, Minn.
items.body:
The Columbus Blue Jackets will seek their first winning streak of the young season on Sunday when they face the Minnesota Wild in Saint Paul, Minn.
Columbus needed overtime on Saturday before skating away with a 1-0 win over the visiting New York Rangers to stop a two-game skid. It was quite the turnaround from the Blue Jackets' previous game on Tuesday, when the visiting Florida Panthers rolled them 7-3.
Defenseman Zach Werenski said after Saturday's win that it wasn't hard to hear the criticism about the team after the lopsided loss. However, the Blue Jackets, along with the Los Angeles Kings, have played the fewest games of any NHL team at six.
"If you really look at the standings, everyone's kind of around the same spot right now, around .500," said Werenski, last season's Norris Trophy winner as the league's top defenseman.
"We didn't want to fall behind that," he continued. "I think we're all aware of how we can play, how we have to play. Like I said, it wasn't perfect tonight but definitely a step in the right direction."
Werenski picked up the primary assist on Kent Johnson's game-winning goal. Johnson leads the team with four goals, and Werenski's five assists are one behind Charlie Coyle's six. Coyle got the secondary helper to maintain the team lead.
The Blue Jackets have scored just 17 goals in six games. However, Wild coach John Hynes said they're a physical team that can cause problems on the attack.
"There's a lot of motion in the offensive zone, a lot of dives and rolls and things like that," Hynes said. "That always presents a challenge because you got to have the awareness to know where guys are going to be because they might not be in areas you think they're going to be."
The Wild have two players who have combined for 14 goals in their eight contests. Kirill Kaprizov leads the NHL with nine goals this season, and Matt Boldy has five.
Kaprizov also is tied for fifth with 14 points. Minnesota defenseman Quinn Hughes has 10 assists, tying him for fourth in the league.
Minnesota has won three of four, beating the St. Louis Blues 5-4 on Thursday. Boldy had a hat trick in the game along with an assist. Kaprizov added a goal and two assists but left the game in the third period after taking a check from Blues goalie Joel Hofer.
Kaprizov did not practice Saturday, but Hynes said it was because the forward was ill.
Hynes' team has gotten off to a strong start this season despite a rash of injuries. That includes defenseman Jared Spurgeon, who has missed the last two games with an upper-body injury, and veteran Nick Foligno, who has been on injured reserve since Oct. 9 with an upper-body injury. Both practiced Saturday, but Hynes does not expect either to suit up Sunday.
Jesper Wallstedt (5-1-1, 2.13 goals-against average, .920 save percentage) will start in goal for Minnesota for the eighth time this season. He faced the Blue Jackets for the first time last season, stopping 27 of 29 shots in a 5-2 win at Columbus on Dec. 18.
With goaltender Jet Greaves getting the shutout Saturday, Columbus may turn to journeyman backup Cam Talbot (1-1, 4.43 GAA, .822 save percentage) on Sunday. In 21 career starts against the Wild, he owns a 9-9-3 record with a 2.64 GAA and .917 save percentage.
--Field Level Media

items.summary: Russia has attacked Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors dozens of times in the week since US President Donald Trump announced a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday.
items.body:
Russia has attacked Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors dozens of times in the week since US President Donald Trump announced a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday.
"Since the American President announced the energy ceasefire a week ago, Russia has deliberately attacked Ukraine's energy and oil and gas sectors 76 times," he wrote on X, adding the latest strikes hit substations in the Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, and Odesa regions.
Neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirmed Trump's announced ceasefire agreement.

items.title: Macron va s'adresser aux Français après les violences en marge des manifestations du 17 octobre
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Emmanuel Macron s'adressera solennellement aux Français dimanche à 20h00, a annoncé l'Elysée au lendemain des scènes de violence et de pillages qui ont terni une journée de vaste mobilisation contre la vie chère dans toute la France.
items.body:
Emmanuel Macron s'adressera solennellement aux Français dimanche à 20h00, a annoncé l'Elysée au lendemain des scènes de violence et de pillages qui ont terni une journée de vaste mobilisation contre la vie chère dans toute la France.
Les maires de Paris, Lyon et Marseille, qui critiquent la gestion du maintien de l'ordre par l'exécutif, doivent être reçus à leur demande par le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, qui a de son côté dénoncé une "violence d'une extrême intensité" organisée par des groupes d'ultragauche rejoints par des délinquants pour "piller et détruire".
Des dégâts importants ont été rapportés dans de nombreuses grandes villes où des centaines de commerces ont été saccagés. La mairie de Limoges a été en grande partie détruite par un incendie.
Initialement né sur les réseaux sociaux, l'appel à manifester le 17 octobre avait été relayé par les syndicats lycéens qui se mobilisent depuis la mi-septembre pour obtenir de meilleures conditions d'enseignement, ainsi que par des organisations syndicales.
Le ministère de l'Intérieur a dénombré 550.000 manifestants dans tout le pays, dont 110.000 à Paris, la CGT faisant état pour sa part de 800.000 personnes dans les cortèges, qui se sont dans l'ensemble déroulés sans incident.
PRINCIPAUX DÉVELOPPEMENTS : 14h30 - Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, annonce sur X un nouveau bilan de plus de 2.000 personnes interpellées et de plus de 600 policiers, gendarmes et pompiers blessés.
12h55 - Dans un communiqué, la Confédération des commerçants de France, qui dit représenter plus de 7.000 TPE du commerce et de l'artisanat dans les centre-villes, estime que près de 1.500 commerces ont été touchés à travers la France samedi.
12h45 - Emmanuel Macron réunira à 17h30 à l'Elysée le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu et les ministres du gouvernement concernés et s'adressera solennellement aux Français à 20h00, annonce l'Elysée.
11h35 - "Je veux des explications et des moyens pour que cela ne se reproduise plus", déclare à la presse le maire socialiste de Marseille, Benoît Payan, alors que le ministre de l'Intérieur est attendu lundi dans la ville. "Mon propos n'est pas d'incriminer la police nationale. La police nationale, elle fait en fonction de qu'on lui demande (...). Je veux savoir quels ordres leurs ont été donnés, je veux savoir s'il leur a été demandé de s'occuper uniquement des manifestants et de lancer des lacrymos sur les manifestants et de ne pas s'occuper des pillages dans la ville."
11h20 - "Pendant une heure, je n'ai pas eu un seul policier national pour protéger la mairie", déclare sur BFM TV Guillaume Guérin, maire LR de Limoges. "On a un problème de soutien de nos forces de l'ordre", ajoute-t-il en déclarant avoir été informé par des policiers qu'ils manquaient de munitions.
11h00 - Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, annonce sur X un bilan de 1.800 personnes interpellées samedi en France et de plus de 500 policiers, gendarmes et pompiers blessés.
10h45 - La secrétaire nationale des Ecologistes Marine Tondelier réclame sur X la démission du ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez, "manifestement dépassé par la situation".
10h12 - "Ce bilan est désastreux car il emporte de lourdes conséquences : d’abord sur les libertés et notamment celle de manifester puisqu’elle est entravée par la violence ; ensuite sur la jeunesse confrontée à la brutalité et privée des réponses attendues du Gouvernement ; enfin sur l’État qui n’a pas été capable d’assurer partout l’ordre public", estime l'ancien président François Hollande dans un message sur X.
09h45 - A Lyon, le préfet du Rhône, Etienne Guyot, fait état de 160 personnes interpellées et placées en garde à vue et d'une centaine de membres des forces de l'ordre blessés.
08h50 - "Nous avons une ville dans une situation de délabrement total", déplore sur franceinfo la première adjointe au maire de Paris, Lamia El Araaje. "Nous avons assisté à des scènes de pillage méthodiques qui n'ont rien à voir avec les revendications sociales."
"A l'évidence, les forces de l'ordre ont été débordées (...) Il y a eu clairement un manque de moyens", dit-elle.
08h15 - Une personne est décédée à la suite d'un arrêt cardiorespiratoire samedi à Paris lors des manifestations contre la vie chère, pendant lesquelles 855 interpellations ont été effectuées, ce qui représente un "chiffre record", déclare la préfecture de police dans un bilan établi à 08h00.
Treize policiers et gendarmes et deux sapeurs-pompiers ont été blessés, ajoute-t-elle.

items.title: Iran's parliament approves Mehrdad Akhlaqi as minister of defence
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Iran's parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi as defence minister on Sunday, ending months of interim leadership at the ministry and placing a former defence sector veteran in charge of the country's defence production and procurement apparatus.
items.body:
Iran's parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi as defence minister on Sunday, ending months of interim leadership at the ministry and placing a former defence sector veteran in charge of the country's defence production and procurement apparatus.
Akhlaqi replaces Majid Ebn al-Reza, who took over in an interim capacity after then Defence Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh was killed by US-Israeli strikes in February.
Akhlaqi has spent decades in Iran's defence industry and has held senior roles in its aerospace and missile sectors. He is subject to US and EU sanctions over his work in Iran's defence sector.
In a programme presented to lawmakers, Akhlaqi pledged to rebuild the country's military-industrial infrastructure, accelerate the development of defence technologies and expand cooperation with private-sector companies.
"If the American enemy makes another miscalculation, the response of the valiant Iranian people and the fighters of Islam will be surprising and extensive," he said, adding that Tehran had taken necessary measures to counter the potential use by the US of its "mother of all bombs" against Iran.
CNN reported this week that the [USN:FWN46108H TEXT:"US has developed"] strike plans that could include using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, also known as the "mother of all bombs", against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if President Donald Trump orders renewed combat operations.
The weapon is the largest non-nuclear bomb in the US arsenal.
"The US President should focus on ensuring his forces are withdrawn safely from our region. If he drops a single bomb, he will have to see how many of his troops end up being carried out of the region in a horizontal position," Akhlaqi said.

items.title: S Africa 11-0 after rain delays start of second test
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: South Africa were 11 for no wicket at lunch after rain curtailed play on the first day of the second test against Australia at St George’s Park on Sunday.
items.body:
South Africa were 11 for no wicket at lunch after rain curtailed play on the first day of the second test against Australia at St George’s Park on Sunday.
Aiden Markram was 10 not out and debutant Marques Ackerman on one as only 5.3 overs were possible in the first session.
Rain delayed the start by two hours after Australia won the toss, with 27 minutes play before the covers came on again and lunch was taken early.
Australia added an extra seamer to their attack with Scott Boland replacing Nathan Lyon.
Kagiso Rabada returns to spearhead the home side’s pace attack after a lengthy injury in place of spinner Keshav Maharaj.
South Africa dropped wicketkeeper Kyle Verreynne with Ryan Rickelton taking the gloves and dropping down the batting ordert from opener to number six.
Australia won the first test in Durban by 214 runs.
items.raw_description: South Africa were 11 for no wicket at lunch after rain curtailed play on the first day of the second test against Australia at St George’s Park on Sunday.

items.title: Rays, Guardians turn to All-Star pitchers in pivotal ALCS Game 5
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: CLEVELAND -- The American League Championship Series has become a best-of-three matchup with the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians splitting the first four games.
items.body:
CLEVELAND -- The American League Championship Series has become a best-of-three matchup with the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians splitting the first four games.
Game 5 will be held Sunday in Cleveland, where Rays right-hander Drew Rasmussen (1-0, 1.29 ERA) takes on Guardians left-hander Parker Messick (0-2, 3.09) in a battle of 2026 All-Star selections.
In ALCS history, the team that takes a 3-2 lead by winning the fifth game has advanced to the World Series 66.7% of the time.
"We've got a huge game, another swing game, and it should be quite the pitching matchup," Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said. "Everything is magnified in the postseason; the big hits, big decisions and the big plays.
"And when you have two teams that are really talented, like we feel both of us are, one play can swing a lot."
The Rays and Guardians have alternated victories, each going 1-1 at home with one rainout in Cleveland. Both also have scored three and seven runs in their wins, illustrating how close the series has been.
Tampa Bay pulled even with a 7-3 triumph Saturday in Game 4, fueled by a combined six hits, five RBIs and four runs from Junior Caminero, Jonathan Aranda and Yandy Diaz. The Rays also forced Cleveland to burn through seven pitchers.
"Our backs have been against the wall before (losing the first two games in the AL Division Series to the Chicago White Sox), so we're not going to just lay down," Guardians pitcher Foster Griffin said. "We feel good with where we're at."
Staff ace Rasmussen started Game 1, giving up two runs on homers to Chase DeLauter and Patrick Bailey in six innings on Oct. 12. He struck out seven without a walk over 91 pitches, taking a no-decision in a 7-3 home loss.
Rasmussen went 1-1 with a 1.50 ERA and 15 strikeouts in 12 innings in two starts against the Guardians during the regular season. He absorbed a road loss to Cleveland on April 29, allowing three runs (two earned) in five innings.
"It's exhausting facing a lineup like this," said Rasmussen, who is 1-1 with a 2.73 ERA in eight career outings (six starts) against the Guardians. "Their bat-to-ball ability is elite and when they get baserunners on, they can all run. They scrap together, every single hitter in that lineup."
Messick wasn't expected to make his next start until the series returned to Tampa Bay, but the Friday rainout put him in play for Game 5. Guardians manager Stephen Vogt noted that using six relievers Saturday made him "need Parker to go for us."
The AL Rookie of the Year contender pitched five innings in Game 2 on Oct. 13, but was saddled with the road loss despite giving up zero earned runs. The Rays plated three unearned runs thanks to an error by third baseman Jose Ramirez.
Messick is in uncharted waters, throwing a lifetime-high 198 innings and 35 starts this year, including playoffs. He hasn't been sharp in three playoff outings, walking eight and allowing 20 baserunners in 11 2/3 innings, but has a terrific track record against Tampa Bay.
In five total starts against the Rays in his two seasons, Messick has only given up three earned runs in 31 1/3 innings for a 0.86 ERA.
"I know I'm soaring well above my career highs, but honestly, my body feels great," he said. "To be able to take the ball in this game shows the confidence the team has in me. It's an incredible blessing."
--Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

items.title: Agenda de la semana: datos de Brasil, Colombia, Argentina y México; resultados de Netflix, Tesla y Meta
items.author: Leidys Becerra
items.summary: La agenda del 19 al 23 de octubre incluye cifras de inflación en Brasil y México, actividad económica en Colombia y Argentina, y ventas minoristas mexicanas. También se conocerán los resultados trimes ...
items.body: La agenda económica de América Latina estará marcada por los datos de actividad económica de Colombia y Argentina, las ventas minoristas de México y los indicadores de inflación de ese país y Brasil. Las cifras permitirán evaluar el ritmo de crecimiento de las principales economías de la región y las presiones sobre los precios. La atención también estará puesta en la campaña presidencial de Brasil. La semana será la última antes de la segunda vuelta del 25 de octubre, en la que se enfrentarán Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva y Flávio Bolsonaro. Las encuestas y los debates televisados serán claves para seguir la evolución de una contienda en la que la diferencia entre los candidatos se ha reducido. Ver más: Los 5 países de América Latina que más dinero atraen en inversión para sus startups, según informe En Estados Unidos se publicarán cifras del mercado inmobiliario, solicitudes iniciales de subsidio por desempleo y datos de confianza del consumidor. La semana también estará marcada por los resultados corporativos de compañías como Netflix, Tesla, Meta Platforms, IBM y ExxonMobil, entre otras. De acuerdo con un informe de Bloomberg Economics elaborado por los economistas Felipe Hernández y Adriana Dupita, junto con la analista Jimena Zúñiga, los datos de la próxima semana ofrecerán nuevas señales sobre la evolución de la actividad económica y la inflación en América Latina. En Colombia, Bloomberg Economics prevé que el indicador de actividad económica registre un crecimiento anual de 2,9% en agosto, aunque con una caída mensual tras el repunte de julio. El informe señala que el terremoto de agosto habría añadido presión a una economía que ya enfrentaba dificultades por la inflación, las tasas de interés elevadas, el menor gasto público y el debilitamiento del mercado laboral. Los riesgos asociados al fenómeno de El Niño también podrían afectar la actividad, mientras que los precios del petróleo y un entorno político más favorable al mercado podrían contribuir a compensar parte de esas presiones. Ver más: Los países donde más crecerán las exportaciones de bienes en América Latina en 2026, según la Cepal México publicará cifras de ventas minoristas e inflación, además de su indicador de actividad económica. Bloomberg Economics espera que las ventas minoristas hayan crecido 1,5% anual en agosto y que la inflación de la primera quincena de octubre se ubique en 3,6% anual. Para el indicador de actividad económica, la estimación es un crecimiento anual de 3,3%, con una expansión mensual más moderada que la registrada en julio. En Argentina, el informe prevé que la actividad económica haya vuelto a crecer en términos anuales en agosto, aunque apenas. La producción industrial y la actividad minera avanzaron 1,9% mensual, mientras que la construcción aumentó 0,4%. Aun así, Bloomberg Economics advierte que la economía podría registrar otra contracción trimestral en el tercer trimestre, lo que implicaría una recesión técnica después de la caída del segundo trimestre. Los analistas consideran, sin embargo, que parte de la volatilidad podría responder a una debilidad temporal y no necesariamente a un deterioro persistente. En Brasil, la inflación de mediados de octubre será el principal dato económico de la semana. Bloomberg Economics espera que los precios continúen mostrando presiones, esta vez impulsadas especialmente por los alimentos y posiblemente por el transporte, mientras que los costos de vivienda podrían permanecer prácticamente estables por la caída de los precios de la electricidad. Ver más: Inflación de septiembre 2026 en América Latina, país por país, de México hasta Argentina Desde las principales ganancias corporativas de EE.UU., incluyendo Meta, Netflix y Tesla, hasta la reunión de ministros de finanzas de APEC en Hong Kong, esto es lo que necesita saber para la próxima semana: *Con información de Bloomberg Economics y Bloomberg.

items.title: China's solar panel exports extend slump in September
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: China's solar power equipment exports fell 6.4% in September from the same month last year, customs data showed on Sunday.
items.body:
China's solar power equipment exports fell 6.4% in September from the same month last year, customs data showed on Sunday.
China, the world's largest solar manufacturer, exported 1.21 million metric tons of solar cells and panels in September. That was down from September a year earlier but up from 840,000 tons in August.
In the year through September, China exported 9.37 million tons of the equipment, down 9.5%.
September solar exports were valued at $3.34 billion, up 19.4%.
On a per-unit basis, China shipped 11.3% more cells and panels, or 1.44 billion.

items.title: Two arrested for terrorism in Spain's Basque Country
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Two people were arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences in Spain's northwestern Basque Country, police said on Sunday.
items.body:
Two people were arrested on suspicion of terrorism offences in Spain's northwestern Basque Country, police said on Sunday.
A 34-year-old man and a woman, 22, who are both Spanish but who have not been named, are under investigation after a police search on September 26.
"Among the items seized was information concerning security forces, as well as the potential location of a site containing materials — presumably weapons and explosives," said a statement from the Ertzaintza, the Basque regional police.
Police did not say if the suspects were held in custody. Both will appear before Spain's National Court at a later date.

items.title: China proposes export controls on solar-manufacturing technologies
items.author: Colleen Howe
items.creator: Colleen Howe
items.summary: China has proposed export controls on 12 technologies used to make solar equipment, citing national security concerns, as part of a broader revision that also covers AI and biotechnology.
items.body:
China has proposed export controls on 12 technologies used to make solar equipment, citing national security concerns, as part of a [USN:P8N44A04L TEXT:"broader revision"] that also covers AI and biotechnology.
The ministry of commerce proposed adding the photovoltaic technologies to China's export-control list, it said in a statement on Friday, adding that greater oversight is needed because solar technologies are increasingly being used in sensitive areas like aerospace and national defense.
Chinese officials held [USN:L1N40Y0TZ TEXT:"initial talks"] with manufacturers about potential curbs on advanced solar-panel manufacturing technologies, Reuters reported in April, a move that could threaten plans by US firms such as Tesla (TSLA.O) to [USN:L6N4080PX TEXT:"expand production"] in the US.
Beijing has also curbed exports of solar-manufacturing technology to [USN:L4N43A1F4 TEXT:"India,"] Reuters has reported. Analysts say China is seeking to preserve its dominance as India tries to build up domestic manufacturing and shake off reliance on China.
Export restrictions aim to "guard against the risks of technologies from running out of control or being improperly disseminated, while safeguarding normal international exchanges and cooperation in science and technology," the ministry said.
Exporters must now register certain overseas technology transfers until the export-control catalogue is formally updated. Public consultation on the proposal will close on November 15.
China would ban technologies including those used to make some thin wafers, perovskite and tandem solar cells, as well as large-scale fluidized-bed polysilicon production technologies.
Perovskite is an emerging technology that offers the potential of increased conversion efficiency. Tandem cells combine perovskite and silicon layers to capture more of the sunlight spectrum.
Fluidized-bed technology for producing polysilicon — a key building block for solar panels — is less expensive and more energy-efficient than the dominant Siemens process.
China would also restrict, but not prohibit, exports of advanced solar cell manufacturing technologies, including TOPCon, HJT and XBC.

items.title: NHL roundup: Panthers make history with third straight natural hat trick
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Carter Verhaeghe scored a natural hat trick as the Florida Panthers made NHL history in an 8-3 rout of the visiting Seattle Kraken on Saturday.
items.body:
Carter Verhaeghe scored a natural hat trick as the Florida Panthers made NHL history in an 8-3 rout of the visiting Seattle Kraken on Saturday.
The Panthers became the first team in NHL history to record natural hat tricks -- three consecutive goals by one player -- in three straight games. Brady Tkachuk accomplished the feat in Florida's previous two outings.
Sam Bennett also tallied three times, while Matthew Tkachuk had three helpers, and younger brother Brady Tkachuk added two for the Panthers, who won their third in a row.
Shane Wright, Frederick Gaudreau and Ryker Evans scored for Seattle, which finished a five-game trip with a 3-1-1 record. Berkly Catton and Kaapo Kakko each had two assists and Joey Daccord stopped 29 of 37 shots.
Flyers 3, Senators 1
Matvei Michkov and Porter Martone each recorded a goal and an assist as Philadelphia defeated visiting Ottawa for its first win of the season.
Dan Vladar made 25 saves for the Flyers, who went 0-6-3 in their first nine contests -- the worst start to a season in franchise history. The Flyers had not scored more than two goals in a game until Trevor Zegras' empty-netter sealed the game in the waning seconds.
Ottawa netminder Linus Ullmark, who came into the contest 6-0-0 on the year, took his first loss despite a steady 25-save effort. Drake Batherson tallied the only goal for the Senators.
Capitals 4, Devils 2
Ilya Protas scored the tiebreaking goal early in the second period for host Washington, which rode a four-goal surge to a win over New Jersey.
Ryan Leonard scored in the first before Dylan Strome and Boone Jenner added goals in the second for the Capitals, who have won two straight. Goaltender Logan Thompson made 29 saves.
Arseny Gritsyuk had a goal in the first and Timo Meier scored in the final minute of the third for the Devils, whose two-game winning streak ended. Goalie Jake Allen recorded 21 saves as New Jersey sustained its fourth multi-goal defeat of the season.
Lightning 4, Canucks 2
Jake Guentzel scored the tiebreaking goal in the third period as Tampa Bay kept its home record clean with a comeback win over Vancouver.
Guentzel, who also had an assist, gave Tampa Bay its first lead at 2:04 of the third period when his long shot deflected off the stick of Vancouver's Liam Ohgren for his fourth goal of the season. Nikita Kucherov tallied twice, and Brayden Point had two assists. Goaltender Dennis Hildeby made 12 saves to help the Lightning improve to 5-0-0 at home this season.
Linus Karlsson and center Elias Pettersson netted for the Canucks, who finished 0-5-1 on their East Coast road trip despite building a 2-0 lead early in the second period. Goalie Kevin Lankinen, who entered with a 6.88 goals-against average, stopped 31 shots.
Hurricanes 3, Jets 2
Nikolaj Ehlers scored the go-ahead power-play goal in the third period as Carolina rallied for its seventh straight victory, defeating host Winnipeg.
Ehlers put Carolina ahead with a power-play slap shot from the high slot at 6:43 of the third period for his first of the season. Mark Jankowski and Jesperi Kotkaniemi also scored, and Shayne Gostisbehere had two assists for the Hurricanes. Pyotr Kochetkov made 21 saves and improved to 5-0-0 on the season.
Mark Scheifele and Alex Iafallo scored for the Jets, who have lost two straight games and three of their last four. Clay Stevenson made 34 saves.
Stars 4, Blackhawks 0
Arttu Hyry scored twice and Jake Oettinger stopped all 19 shots he faced for his third shutout of the season as Dallas topped host Chicago and improved to 4-1-1 since losing its first two games of the season.
Jason Robertson also scored and assisted on Roope Hintz's third-period goal. Hyry, who totaled three goals in 25 games spanning the past two seasons with the Stars, has already matched that total in eight games to open this season.
Oettinger was hardly tested by the Blackhawks, who went 0-for-4 on the power play. Oettinger has allowed just six goals on 126 shot attempts while 3-2-1 on the young season. Spencer Knight made 28 saves for Chicago, which lost for the first time in three games with star Connor Bedard back in the lineup from shoulder surgery.
Red Wings 4, Sharks 3 (SO)
Lucas Raymond had the only goal during a shootout as host Detroit rallied past San Jose.
The Red Wings' Alex DeBrincat scored with 1:33 left in regulation to send the game into overtime. Emmitt Finnie had a goal and an assist, Justin Faulk also scored and Moritz Seider notched two assists for Detroit, which has won two in a row. John Gibson made 31 saves.
San Jose star Macklin Celebrini racked up a goal and two assists, Dmitry Orlov and Ivar Stenberg supplied power-play goals and Stenberg added an assist. Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 24 shots for the Sharks, who fell to 1-2-1 in their past four games.
Blue Jackets 1, Rangers 0 (OT)
Kent Johnson scored with 1:34 remaining in overtime as Columbus finally solved rookie goaltender Dylan Garand and earned a victory over visiting New York.
Johnson scored for the third straight game by teaming up with Charlie Coyle and Zach Werenski for the game-winner. Blue Jackets goalie Jet Greaves made 29 saves for his fifth career shutout. He was flawless after allowing 11 goals in his first four appearances of the season.
Garand finished with 28 saves, but his performance was not enough to prevent the Rangers from consecutive losses for the first time this season. The goalie was significantly better than in the 7-1 loss in New Jersey on Thursday when he was pulled after allowing four goals on 13 shots.
Canadiens 4, Sabres 3 (OT)
Cole Caufield scored his second goal of the game 54 seconds into overtime, lifting Montreal past visiting Buffalo for its third win in four games.
Seconds after the Sabres' Josh Norris missed the net on a 3-on-1, the puck rolled down the left side and Caufield collected it to break in and beat Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen bar down. Zachary Bolduc and Alexandre Texier also scored for the Canadiens, Juraj Slafkovsky and Alexandre Carrier each had two assists, and Jacob Fowler made 23 saves.
Norris, Jack Quinn and Tage Thompson scored for Buffalo, which earned a point for the fourth consecutive game (2-0-2). Luukkonen stopped 30 shots.
Predators 5, Blues 2
Filip Forsberg scored his first goal of the season and added an assist for Nashville, which also scored on a penalty kill and a penalty shot in a victory over visiting St. Louis.
Jonathan Marchessault, Adam Edstrom, Ryan O'Reilly and Jack Drury also scored for the Predators. Steven Stamkos, Adam Wilsby and Roman Josi each recorded two assists. Juuse Saros made 24 saves for Nashville, which snapped a three-game winless streak (0-1-2).
The Blues got goals from Philip Broberg and Jimmy Snuggerud. Mason McTavish, Jake Neighbours and Dylan Holloway added assists. Jordan Binnington stopped 19 shots for the Blues, who lost their second straight.
Islanders 4, Maple Leafs 1
New York secured its first road win of the season with a victory over Toronto to improve to 1-2-1 away from home.
Anthony Duclair and Bo Horvat put the Islanders up 2-0 after 40 minutes and Simon Holmstrom rounded out the win with a pair of goals in the game's final six minutes. Ilya Sorokin continued his hot start, turning away 28 shots in his fourth win of the season.
Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 16 of 19 shots for the Maple Leafs, who got a goal from Colton Sissons.Toronto has allowed three-plus goals in seven consecutive games and has lost three straight.
Bruins 4, Kings 1
David Pastrnak and Marat Khusnutdinov each had a goal and an assist for visiting Boston in a win over Los Angeles.
Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka scored empty-net goals and Jeremy Swayman made 25 saves for the Bruins, who have won five in a row, including a 4-2 win at the Anaheim Ducks on Friday night.
Alex Laferriere scored and Anton Forsberg made 24 saves for the Kings, who fell to 0-4-2. Los Angeles' winless start is its longest since opening the 1984-85 season with a 0-6-3 record.
Golden Knights 6, Penguins 2
Mark Stone scored a goal and had two assists and Trevor Connelly added a goal and an assist as Vegas cruised past Pittsburgh in Las Vegas for its third consecutive victory.
Rasmus Andersson, Noah Hanifin, Shea Theodore and Brett Howden also scored and Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner each added two assists for the Golden Knights, who had won their previous game, at home against Calgary, by the same 6-2 score. Adin Hill finished with 22 saves to improve to 4-0-0.
Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin scored, Tommy Novak had two assists and Sergei Murashov finished with 14 saves for the Penguins, who lost their third straight and sixth in seven games.
Oilers 6, Mammoth 2
Connor McDavid scored twice and added three assists as Edmonton thumped Utah in Salt Lake City.
Leon Draisaitl tallied and added an assist. Zach Hyman, Mathieu Joseph and Kasperi Kapanen also scored for the Oilers, who have earned points in seven of their eight games. Vasily Podkolzin chipped in two assists, and Tristan Jarry made 26 saves.
John Marino and Mikhail Sergachev responded with third-period goals for the Mammoth, who saw their three-game winning streak end. Karel Vejmelka allowed five goals on 17 shots before being replaced by Sebastian Cossa at 13:48 of the second period.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Trump dispose d'un délai pour se prononcer sur les sanctions contre la Russie, dit Rubio
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le secrétaire d'Etat américain Marco Rubio a déclaré samedi que Donald Trump disposait d'un délai pouvant aller jusqu'à 60 jours pour évaluer l'impact économique des sanctions et des droits de douane liés à la Russie.
items.body:
Le secrétaire d'Etat américain Marco Rubio a déclaré samedi que Donald Trump disposait d'un délai pouvant aller jusqu'à 60 jours pour évaluer l'impact économique des sanctions et des droits de douane liés à la Russie.
Le président américain a déclaré samedi qu'il devait encore annoncer une décision définitive sur la question, un jour après avoir décidé de lever plusieurs sanctions visant Moscou dans le cadre d'une loi promulguée le mois dernier.
"Beaucoup d'entre vous ne connaissent pas encore ma décision, mais nous y verrons clair, et vous y verrez clair", a déclaré Donald Trump aux journalistes depuis sa résidence de Mar-a-Lago, en Floride.
La suspension des sanctions américaines intervient à quelques semaines seulement des élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis.
Donald Trump est confronté au mécontentement des Américains en raison des prix élevés de l'énergie alors que la guerre avec l'Iran perturbant l'approvisionnement mondial en pétrole.
Le locataire de la Maison blanche a publié vendredi un décret prévoyant la levée des sanctions, mais le texte ne précisait pas la durée de cette dérogation.
Marco Rubio a indiqué que Donald Trump avait opté pour une période d'examen de 60 jours.
"Je pense que le président souhaite profiter de ce délai de 60 jours pour analyser en quelque sorte les conséquences que l'imposition à la fois de sanctions et de droits de douane aurait sur l'économie mondiale, voire sur l'économie américaine", a-t-il dit.
Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky s'est élevé contre la publication du décret, estimant que cela encouragerait son homologue russe Vladimir Poutine et prolongerait la guerre.

items.title: German police investigate fence breach at Leipzig airport
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: German police said on Sunday that they were investigating a breach at the Leipzig/Halle airport after a vehicle appeared to drive through a fence, in a second security lapse this year.
items.body:
German police said on Sunday that they were investigating a breach at the Leipzig/Halle airport after a vehicle appeared to drive through a fence, in a second security lapse this year.
In August, investigators discovered [USN:L8N4420IV TEXT:"an explosive-laden drone"] near a runway at the airport, an event that German officials later said [USN:L8N44T1N2 TEXT:"Russia was responsible"] for. Russia has denied the allegations.
One runway has been closed, but passenger traffic was running as normal on Sunday, an airport spokesperson said.
German police first responded to the suspected breach late on Saturday evening.
Leipzig police earlier said they hadn't found suspicious objects or unauthorized personnel but would be carrying out further searches.
Police at the scene on Sunday were looking for clues in the area around a large break in the chain-link and barbed-wire fence.
Germany ordered a series of measures in response to August's attempted drone attack, including the closure of a consulate and a Russian cultural centre in Berlin.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Saturday addressed security issues when speaking to party members. "The threat for us all is very real," he said.

items.title: Lithuania tells residents to go to shelters after detecting suspected drone
items.author: Andrius Sytas
items.creator: Andrius Sytas
items.summary: Lithuania told residents in central and northern parts of the country to seek shelter for about an hour on Sunday morning after an unidentified flying object entered its airspace, the army and national crisis management centre said.
items.body:
Lithuania told residents in central and northern parts of the country to seek shelter for about an hour on Sunday morning after an unidentified flying object entered its airspace, the army and national crisis management centre said.
The object was likely a drone which entered from Poland, Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas told reporters, adding that he had proposed a joint investigation with his Polish counterpart.
Poland's military said it was also [USN:FWN4630JH TEXT:"verifying a possible violation of its airspace"] by an unidentified object. A Polish defence ministry spokesperson later said radar systems did not confirm the object crossing the border into Lithuania, but added that Polish authorities were remaining in contact with Lithuanian officials.
NATO SCRAMBLES FIGHTERS During the "red" alert, NATO fighter jets were scrambled to the area, and Kaunas airport, near Lithuania's second-largest city, was temporarily closed, the crisis management centre said.
The NATO aircraft were unable to visually identify the object due to cloudy weather and did not attempt to shoot it down, the centre said.
Lithuanian army personnel were investigating possible drone debris near Juodzionys village in northern Lithuania, after the object disappeared from radar, the centre said.
Some of the debris struck a civilian vehicle, Kaunas said.
"We can confirm that two Italian Eurofighter jets were scrambled earlier today in response to a drone over Lithuanian airspace," a NATO official said.
"The aircraft were operating under NATO command. An investigation is ongoing, and NATO remains in close contact with the Lithuanian authorities," the official said, adding that the alliance was ready and able to react to any potential threat.
Northern neighbour Latvia briefly issued a "yellow" air warning in some regions bordering Lithuania, citing a "possible threat", its army said.
Ukrainian drones have repeatedly [USN:L8N41X1AC TEXT:"entered NATO airspace"] in the Baltic region in recent months. Kyiv has said they were steered off course by Russian signal jamming.
This has stoked concerns that Russia's war in Ukraine is spilling over NATO's borders.

items.title: Vietnam signs free-trade pact with European countries including Norway, Switzerland
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Norway, Switzerland, Iceland and Liechtenstein have signed a free-trade agreement with Vietnam, the governments of Norway and Vietnam announced on Sunday.
items.body:
Norway, Switzerland, Iceland and Liechtenstein have signed a free-trade agreement with Vietnam, the governments of Norway and Vietnam announced on Sunday.
Vietnam's trade ministry said it signed the deal in Hanoi with the European Free Trade Association members.
Around half of Norway's exports to Vietnam will be tariff-free when the agreement enters into force, with more than 98% to be tariff-free within seven years, the Norwegian government said in a statement.
Long-stalled free-trade talks were [USN:L6N4600OA TEXT:"relaunched last year"] amid global tensions over US tariffs. [USN:L8N4340QC TEXT:"Negotiations concluded"] in July.
Vietnam's trade ministry said the Southeast Asian country mainly exports seafood, footwear, textiles, machinery and equipment, electronics and components to the EFTA market and imports industrial machinery and equipment, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and raw materials for production.
Bilateral trade between Vietnam and EFTA member countries has averaged $2 billion annually, the ministry said.

items.title: Campeón Cruz Azul golea a Bravos Ciudad Juárez en torneo mexicano
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Cruz Azul, vigente campeón del fútbol mexicano, goleó el sábado 4-0 a Bravos de Ciudad Juárez en la duodécima jornada del torneo Apertura.
items.body:
Cruz Azul, vigente campeón del fútbol mexicano, goleó el sábado 4-0 a Bravos de Ciudad Juárez en la duodécima jornada del torneo Apertura.
La "Máquina Celeste" de Cruz Azul subió del séptimo al quinto lugar general con 20 puntos, dentro de la zona que da acceso a la postemporada. Los primeros ocho lugares al término de las 17 jornadas de la fase regular obtienen ese boleto.
En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, Cruz Azul se adelantó a los cuatro minutos cuando Andrés Montaño remató de zurda en el área chica un centro enviado por el argentino Agustín Palavecino.
La "Máquina Celeste" aumentó su ventaja a los 23 minutos con un remate de Carlos Rodríguez tras centro enviado por Alan Mozo desde el sector derecho.
Omar Campos anotó el tercer gol en tiempo de reposición de la primera parte cuando definió de zurda ante la salida del portero tras recibir un pase de Montaño.
Cruz Azul siguió presionando en la segunda parte y anotó el cuarto gol a los 54 minutos cuando Palavecino aprovechó un error defensivo para robar el balón y meterlo pegado al poste izquierdo.
El quinto gol cayó a los 75 con un potente disparo de Rogelio González desde fuera del área.
En los otros partidos disputados el sábado, América se consolidó como el líder general tras golear 5-3 de visita a León. Las "Águilas" del América llegaron a 24 puntos en la cima de la tabla general, donde le siguen Toluca y Atlas con 21 unidades.
Por su parte, Santos Laguna registró su quinto triunfo consecutivo al vencer 5-0 a Querétaro.
En tanto, Guadalajara y Tigres UANL empataron 1-1.
La jornada concluirá el domingo cuando Monterrey reciba a Pachuca.
El viernes, Pumas UNAM ganó 2-1 de visita al Atlante, Atlas derrotó 2-0 de visita a Necaxa, y Tijuana y Puebla empataron 0-0.

items.title: Golden Knights keep rolling, add to Penguins' struggles
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Mark Stone scored a goal and had two assists and Trevor Connelly added a goal and an assist as the Vegas Golden Knights cruised to their third straight victory, 6-2, over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Saturday night in Las Vegas.
items.body:
Mark Stone scored a goal and had two assists and Trevor Connelly added a goal and an assist as the Vegas Golden Knights cruised to their third straight victory, 6-2, over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Saturday night in Las Vegas.
Rasmus Andersson, Noah Hanifin, Shea Theodore and Brett Howden also scored and Jack Eichel and Mitch Marner each added two assists for the Golden Knights.
Adin Hill finished with 22 saves to improve to 4-0-0.
Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin scored, Tommy Novak had two assists and Sergei Murashov finished with 14 saves for Pittsburgh, which lost its third straight and sixth in seven games.
Vegas jumped out to a 3-0 lead in the first period, scoring twice in the first 4:02. Andersson started the scoring 66 seconds into the contest when he ripped a wrist shot while cutting down the slot past Murashov's glove side for his second goal of 2026-27.
Three minutes later, Hanifin followed with his second goal of the season, taking a crossing pass from Eichel in the left circle and then firing a wrist shot into the bottom left corner.
Stone extended the lead to 3-0 at the 17:46 mark with a power-play goal, redirecting a Connelly shot on the backdoor by the left post that caromed in off his skate for his team-leading seventh goal.
Pittsburgh, playing the second game of a back-to-back that began with a 5-2 loss at Colorado on Friday, cut the lead to 3-1 early in the second. Crosby, stationed by the right post on the power play, redirected Novak's shot past Hill for his third goal.
The Golden Knights responded with two goals in just over four minutes to extend the lead to 5-1. Connelly got the first, intercepting a Crosby pass near the blue line and then rushing down the left wing and snapping a wrist shot past Murashov glove-side. Theodore followed with his second goal this season on a slap shot from the right circle.
Malkin made it 5-2 early in the third when he jammed in a rebound for his team-leading fifth goal this season.
Howden finished the scoring with 2:13 remaining when he was awarded a goal after getting dragged down by Kris Letang while skating toward an empty net.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Rubio heads to Central Asia while other US officials hit foreign policy hot spots
items.author: Gram Slattery, Simon Lewis
items.creator: Gram Slattery, Simon Lewis
items.summary: While the Iran war smolders, Saudi Arabia fights the Houthis and a new rift opens in US-Ukraine relations, Secretary of State Marco Rubio travels on Sunday to Uzbekistan, a nation far removed from the biggest US foreign policy challenges.
items.body:
While the Iran war smolders, Saudi Arabia fights the Houthis and a new rift opens in US-Ukraine relations, Secretary of State Marco Rubio travels on Sunday to Uzbekistan, a nation far removed from the biggest US foreign policy challenges.
The top US diplomat is scheduled to land in Samarkand on Sunday to meet with leaders from the C5+1, a grouping that brings together the United States and the Muslim-majority post-Soviet states of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.
US officials have portrayed resource-rich Central Asia — the region between China, Russia and Iran — as worthy of more attention than it received from US President Donald Trump's predecessors.
Trump hosted C5 leaders at the White House last November, when Kazakhstan agreed to join the Abraham Accords, a series of agreements under which Muslim-majority countries have normalized or deepened relations with Israel. Separately, Trump met with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the United Nations General Assembly last September.
Regional politics aside, the trip fits an emerging pattern in which Rubio often visits regions not at the center of the news cycle, while leaving some more fraught foreign-policy portfolios to other Trump aides, including special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Vice President JD Vance.
For instance, Rubio has not visited Kyiv or Moscow since becoming secretary of state. He was not present for talks between US and Ukrainian officials in Florida earlier this month, when US officials pressed Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries. Vance, not Rubio, represented the US in Pakistan during peace talks with Iran in April.
Rubio's previous foreign trip, in early October, took him to Greece, Portugal and Iceland.
Trump administration officials have typically rejected any suggestion that cabinet-level officials should focus their travels on geopolitical capitals and hot spots.
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, for instance, said on X last week that the idea only certain destinations were worthy of visits from secretaries of state "perfectly encapsulates the decadence and degeneracy of the contemporary US foreign policy establishment."
US-RUSSIA RELATIONS LOOM One Central Asian diplomat, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said officials in the region are wondering to what extent the US will continue targeting Russian sanctions evasion. All C5 states, while drawing closer to the US, have deep historical ties with Moscow, and the region has facilitated Russian imports and exports that violate US and European Union sanctions, Western officials say.
In the past, the US has pushed regional states to clamp down on those illicit flows.
But Trump struck a deal with Moscow this month to [USN:L1N45Y0GJ TEXT:"import Russian diesel"], a move to lower domestic fuel prices before the congressional midterm elections. On Friday, Trump [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"waived"] all provisions of legislation that would have allowed him to slap massive tariffs on some nations that buy significant amounts of Russian crude or otherwise help Moscow evade sanctions. Among the nations that could have been affected, experts have said, are India and Kazakhstan.
India, which Rubio will visit after Uzbekistan, remains the world's No. 2 Russian crude importer after China, despite Trump saying in February that India had agreed to stop buying oil from Russia.
Additional questions hang over a potential trade deal with India and an expansion of the Abraham Accords in Central Asia.
A US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, described the trade deal on Friday as "pretty much done," raising the possibility that an agreement could be announced during the Rubio trip.
Separately, the US [USN:L1N3TQ0WH TEXT:"has talked to"] additional Central Asian nations about joining the Abraham Accords, Reuters reported last year, conversations that could in theory continue in Samarkand.
More than 200 business executives will accompany Rubio to Uzbekistan, the State Department said. The Central Asian diplomat said the Trump administration has focused its commercial efforts on expanding access to the area's rare earth mineral resources.
The trip to Uzbekistan was largely organized by Sergio Gor, the US ambassador to India, the Central Asian diplomat said. Gor, who was born in Uzbekistan and is a friend of Rubio, also serves as the US special envoy for South and Central Asian affairs.
After Uzbekistan, Rubio will visit the Indian cities of Mumbai and Jamnagar to meet with business leaders, including Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) Chairman Mukesh Ambani, who earned the Trump administration's favor earlier in the year by backing a new refinery in Texas. Rubio most recently visited India five months ago.
The trip is due to wrap up on Thursday.

items.title: Cepal revela qué países se beneficiarán por mejoras en precios en la región: de Perú a Venezuela
items.author: Juan Pablo Álvarez
items.summary: El organismo prevé una notoria mejora en los términos de intercambio para la mayoría de economías de Latinoamérica y Caribe.
items.body: Los términos de intercambio de América Latina y el Caribe aumentarían un 6% en 2026, según proyecta un informe de la Comisión Económica para América Latina y el Caribe (CEPAL). Esta mejora refleja el mayor crecimiento de los precios de exportación respecto de los precios de importación, lo que incrementa la capacidad de compra externa de la región y contribuye positivamente a los ingresos generados por el comercio internacional. VER MÁS: Los países donde más crecerán las exportaciones de bienes en América Latina en 2026, según la Cepal Las mayores ganancias se observarían en el Perú (26%) y Venezuela (23%), seguidas por las de Bolivia (18%), Jamaica (16%), Trinidad y Tobago (15%) y Guyana (14%), impulsadas principalmente por el aumento de los precios de los hidrocarburos y otros productos básicos Por el contrario, algunas economías centroamericanas y caribeñas experimentarían deterioros o mejoras marginales. Entre los que sufrirían un empeoramiento de las condiciones de intercambio aparecen: Honduras (-4%), Haití (-1%), Barbados (-1%). Esta sería la variación en términos de intercambio en cada país de América Latina y el Caribe, según Cepal: “América del Sur aparece como la principal beneficiaria del actual ciclo de precios, con un crecimiento proyectado de las exportaciones del 17%, que obedecería a un aumento de los precios de exportación (15%), mientras que los volúmenes crecerían un 2%”, reseña el estudio de Cepal. Y agrega: “Esta composición refleja la elevada especialización de la subregión en recursos naturales y productos básicos, cuyos precios han experimentado alzas generalizadas”.
